rows.en: Don't answer; let it ring

{f:I|I} picked up the receiver.
"...Hello, this is {a}."
"Oh, {a}{f:|}? It's me!"
"Huh?"
The voice was strangely overfamiliar.
Who on earth was it?
"Aw, come on, have you forgotten me already? We were together just a little while ago."{p}

"Oh! Hosoda."
"Wow, you remembered me. That makes me happy.
Actually, there's something I want to talk to you about. Will you hear me out?"
"Uh, s-sure..."
"Thanks. I just knew you'd hear me out.
You remember Mr. Kuroki's story from earlier, right?"
"Yes."
"Well, even after I got home, I couldn't stop thinking about that wall.
Whether there really is an air-raid shelter behind it, you know?"{p}

...Had Hosoda really gone to the trouble of calling just to tell me that{f:?|?}
And how did {f:he|he} know {f:my|my} phone number?
{f:I|I} was sure I had never {f:given|given} it to him.
"...Hello? Hello?
What's wrong? Are you listening?"
"Oh, uh, yes."
"So, this is hard to ask, but what do you say?
Why don't we go together, right now, and check what's behind that wall?"
"What?! Right now?"
What on earth was he {f:going on about|talking about}?
It was almost eleven o'clock, and he wanted to go to school now...?{p}What should I do?
How should I {f:answer|answer}?
Let's do it tomorrow
Sorry, but I'm not interested
All right. I'll come now

"...Um, it's already late tonight, so why don't we do it tomorrow?"
I thought that would get me off the hook.
I had no intention whatsoever of doing it tomorrow; I thought I'd turned him down politely.
But on the other end of the line, Hosoda got worked up and raised his voice.
"What are you talking about, {a}?! Tomorrow's too late!
If we go there in the daytime, how are we supposed to see what's behind the wall?
It has to be at night! Now's our only chance!"
Hosoda's voice was strangely rough.
I could even hear his heavy breathing clearly.{p}...What should I do?
All right. I'll come now
Give it a rest, please. I'm sleepy!
Tell him to go alone and hang up

"...All right. I'll come now."
Even if I turned him down here, Hosoda would surely keep pestering {f:me|me} until I {f:gave|gave} in.
Left with no choice, {f:I|I} gave him that answer.
"Thank you!
Thank you, {a}{f:|}!
I just knew you'd say that!
Well then, I'll be waiting at the school gate an hour from now. See you there!"
"Ah, wait a minu..."{p}
As soon as he'd said all he wanted to say, Hosoda hung up.{p}
"...{f:Oh, man|Oh, great}."{p}

I didn't think I was late, but Hosoda was already waiting at the school gate.
"{a}{f:|}!"
When Hosoda spotted {f:me|me}, he came running over, looking delighted.
A big bag hung from his shoulder.
What on earth could be in it{f:?|?}
"Come on, let's go to the old school building.
And find out what's behind that wall!"
Hosoda's eyes were gleaming wildly.
Why he was so obsessed with this that he'd go to such lengths, {f:I|I} couldn't understand.{p}

{f:We|We} headed for the old school building.
Was Mr. Kuroki asleep by now{f:?|?}{p}

Sure enough, the wall was a different color.
Maybe this was the spot.
"Right."
Hosoda lowered the big, heavy-looking bag from his shoulder and set it on the floor.
Judging by the way the floor creaked, it had to be really heavy.
When he unzipped it, a lump of metal emerged from inside.
"Hosoda, this is...!"
{f:I|I} couldn't help crying out.
Hosoda smiled happily and took the lump out.{p}

"Heh heh... My dad's hobby is DIY, see.
So I borrowed his power saw."
{f:I|I} was left gaping.
Surely he wasn't going to hack this wall apart with a power saw{f:?|?}{p}What should {f:I|I} do?
Stop him
Keep quiet and watch

"Hosoda, stop it!"
Hosoda shoved {f:me|me} away with tremendous force.
"What do you think you're doing?!
We're about to see an incredible secret!
I can feel it, you know! I can really feel it!
A mighty grudge is swirling around in there!
Nothing but bad things have happened at this school since way back.
There's an evil spirit here!
And it's sleeping in there!
Hyaaaaaa-hahahahaaa!"
"...Hosoda."
{f:I|I} couldn't stop him anymore.
Caught in the round glow of the flashlight, Hosoda's eyes were bloodshot, and he was cackling.{p}
Hosoda didn't care; he kept swinging the saw around, widening the hole in the wall.{p}

"Gyaaah!"
Suddenly, Hosoda was blown backward.
The power saw, still running as if alive, went flying and danced around, bouncing across the floor.
"Hosoda!"
{f:I|I} hurriedly picked up the flashlight and shone it on Hosoda's face.
"{f:Whoa|Eek}!"
{f:I|I} fell right on my backside, my legs giving out beneath me.{p}

Hosoda's face was so badly burned it was no longer recognizable, and faint wisps of steam rose from it.
As if he'd been hit by a flamethrower at close range...
Was this hellfire...?
But I hadn't seen any fire...
"Ugh... ah..."
Even so, Hosoda was still alive.
Blood flowing from burned, torn-apart vessels dripped onto the gooey, melted shreds of flesh.
And he was trying to scoop that blood up and put it back, with hands that were burned raw too, white bone showing here and there.
But his palms were already riddled with holes and could not hold the blood; every effort ended, uselessly, in vain.
"...Look what you've done."
A voice rang out behind me.{p}

When I turned around, Mr. Kuroki was there.
Mr. Kuroki was glaring fixedly at the gaping hole.
"...Sir."
Even when {f:I|I} called out to him, he didn't seem to hear.
"...The soldiers will come out.
To teach a lesson to the fools of today, who sit back so smugly on top of their corpses."
Mr. Kuroki didn't so much as glance at Hosoda or {f:me|me}.
Then he walked slowly toward the power saw and picked it up as it thrashed about.
And he raised it high.{p}

"Die!"
With that, the teacher turned to face {f:me|me}.
"M... Mr. Kuroki..."
I tried to scream, but only a trembling voice as faint as a mosquito's whine came out.
The teacher took aim at {f:me|me} and raised the power saw high.
...{f:Did|No way... Did} {f:he take me for a soldier|I look like a soldier's ghost to him}?
The wall the power saw had hacked apart gaped open like a devil's mouth.
What was {f:inside|inside} that hole{f:?|?}
Was there really an air-raid shelter {f:in there|in there}...?
Without ever finding out, {f:I|I} would fall prey to those sharp teeth and lose my life in just a few more seconds.
Behind the teacher, his hair flying wildly, a host of soldiers' ghosts rose up... or was that {f:just my imagination|just my imagination}...?{p}

{f:I|I} had laid hands on something forbidden{f:.|.}
A world humans are better off not knowing...{p}
The sharp teeth that cut flesh and crush bone came swinging down on {f:my|my} head.{p}

"Well, actually... um, you see, {f:we|we}... uh, hmm..."
{f:I|I} desperately tried to think of an excuse.
But nothing came to mind on the spot.
Mr. Kuroki glared at {f:me|me}.
"It's no use trying to fool me.
Don't do something so cowardly!"
He bellowed it at me.
{f:I|I} shrank back in spite of myself.
"I-I'm {f:sorry|sorry}..."
"You'll tell me what you were up to, won't you?"
There was no way I could lie to this teacher.
{f:I|I} decided to tell the truth.{p}

As {f:I|I} bowed my head and said so, the teacher looked at me with disappointment.
"I see... It's an interesting story, though."{p}

"Is it more interesting than Hanako-san?"
Hosoda asked.
He must {f:really|really} love this kind of story.
His eyes were sparkling with anticipation.
"Sure it is.
After all, it really happened."
The teacher nodded.{p}

"I want to hear it.
Hey, {a}{f:|}, why don't we listen to his story?
It's a rare chance, after all."
"Uh..."
{f:I|I} hesitated.{p}What should I do?
I don't want to hear it
I don't mind hearing it
"But it's already late. Let's leave it for tomorrow after all."{p}

"What, you're such a buzzkill."
Hosoda sulked.
"Then you can go home by yourself, {a}{f:|}.
Please tell us, sir."
"Sure, why not."
The teacher nodded casually.
Hosoda turned to {f:me|me}.{p}

"Bye then, {a}{f:|}. See ya."
Easy for him to say...{p}Was it really okay for me to go home alone{f:?|?}
He said I can, so go home
Stay and listen after all
{f:I|I} decided to go home.{p}
It was a shame to miss the story, but I had a feeling it was for the best{f:.|.}{p}

Carrying that nameless unease, {f:I|I} didn't sleep a wink until morning came.
Ignoring my family, who were surprised to see {f:me|me} up on my own, I dashed out of the house.
Even in the morning sun, the unease didn't fade.
Something must have happened.
{f:I|I} just knew it.{p}

{f:I|I} went to the second-year classroom.
But Hosoda hadn't come in.
The second-year who told me so looked puzzled.
"Weird. He was always so proud of never being late or absent."
Maybe he'd stayed at the old school building late last night and was short on sleep{f:?|?}
Mr. Kuroki had seemed like a pretty fun-loving guy, too.
When {f:I|I} said that, the senior frowned.
"Kuroki? Who's that? He's not a teacher here."
"Huh? But... wasn't he on night duty?"
"Never heard of him.
I'm pretty sure there's no teacher called Kuroki at our school."
{f:I|I} had no idea what was going on.{p}

The teacher was in the connecting corridor.
"Mr. Kuroki?"
As the teacher heard {f:my|my} story, the teacher's expression clouded over.
"Nobody's seen Hosoda since last night, either... I feel like something bad is happening."
In answer to {f:my|my} plea, the teacher spoke.
"Just forget about it..."
For a moment, I couldn't believe my ears.{p}

It wasn't just Hosoda.
There were the people who had disappeared, too.
And yet...
The teacher didn't seem the least bit surprised.{p}

As {f:I|I} stood there stunned, the teacher went on.
"There's no teacher named Kuroki at this school.
But Mr. Kuroki definitely exists."
"...What do you mean?"
"Mr. Kuroki is... a {g}'Thing' that has lived in this school since long ago."
With that, the teacher explained.{p}

That since long before the new school building was built, strange incidents had been happening at this school.
And that a person called {g}"Mr. Kuroki" was always involved in those incidents.
But Mr. Kuroki was not human.
He was a mysterious being who spirited students and teachers away to who knows where.{p}

"Something that infests this school, or the school's own will... That's what I suspect it is, anyway."
The teacher gave {f:me|me} a pat on the shoulder.
"That can't be..."
I couldn't believe it.
But in a way, it also made a strange kind of sense.{p}

"Sir... So does the school know about Mr. Kuroki?"
"No, most of the teachers probably don't.
I'm a graduate of this school, you see.
I found out about Mr. Kuroki while I was a student here.
That's why I came back as a teacher."
I couldn't accept that explanation.
I mean, there were just far too many incidents{f:.|.}
I couldn't believe the other teachers {f:hadn't|hadn't} noticed.
So {f:I|I} asked.
"Hasn't the principal noticed either?"
At that, the teacher held a finger to the lips.
{f:That must have meant|It meant} 'Be quiet.'
A small voice, almost a whisper.
"Several incidents happen every year, but the number of new students never drops, right?
Apparently, if we look the other way while Mr. Kuroki takes a few, hundreds of times that many students enroll."
"So... that's why you leave Mr. Kuroki alone?"
The teacher nodded.
Was it something like a zashiki-warashi, the spirit said to make a house prosper{f:?|?}
But I'd never heard of a zashiki-warashi that wanted sacrifices{f:.|.}
Was it really okay not to tell the police{f:?|?}
I suddenly noticed the teacher was standing right next to me.
As if reading {f:my|my} thoughts, the teacher gave a quiet shake of the head.
"You must not go against this school.
I don't know what happened to the people who vanished... but this is something that can cover up incidents like that without batting an eye."{p}
The moment those words were spoken, the windowpane beside us gave a sharp crack.{p}

"{a}, stop this pointless prying."
The teacher hurriedly grabbed {f:my|my} shoulder.
The teacher's face had gone pale.
"B-but..."
"Do you want to die★"{p}

And then I understood.
The teacher was right{f:.|.}{p}

{f:I|I} nodded slowly.
"I understand... I'll forget all about this."
"Good."
The teacher smiled, looking relieved.{p}

The next instant, the glass shattered and spilled to the ground like a waterfall.
The high, clear sound of breaking rained down on {f:me|me}.
As if frozen time had suddenly started moving again.
Listening to it, {f:I|I} was overcome with a sense of defeat.
{f:I|I} had lost{f:.|.}
To this school.
To Mr. Kuroki, lurking in that darkness... no, to something even more evil.
But maybe I should be glad that at least I hadn't been swallowed by the darkness like Hosoda.
Forcing myself to believe that, {f:I|I} set off walking with the teacher.
...Behind my back, I heard someone's mocking laughter.{p}

"All right. Let's hear it."
{f:I|I} nodded.{p}

"That's our {a}{f:|}!"
Hosoda looked {f:pleased|pleased}.{p}

That's right, there was a classroom back there.
Just an ordinary classroom, you ask?
...No, of course not.
In the middle of the classroom floor, there was a trapdoor.{p}

Beneath it was an air-raid shelter.
A small one, only big enough for five or six people at most.
Maybe nobody ever seriously meant to use it.
Even at thirty to a class, by the numbers five out of six wouldn't make it.
Apparently there was a proper shelter for the students somewhere else.
So even though it was wartime, it had never actually been used.
Yes... not until that day...{p}

During the war, there were often air raids around here too.
What did people do at times like that, you ask?
There was nothing they could do.
The enemy was in airplanes.
All they could do was hide in a shelter and wait for them to pass.{p}

One day, the students were at work making ammunition.
It may have been a school, but during the war they were apparently made to do nothing but that kind of work instead of studying.
Then the air-raid siren went off.
Everyone hurried to the shelter as usual.{p}

But just then, there was an explosion nearby.
A bomb had scored a direct hit on the school building.{p}

When they came to, most of their classmates were no longer moving.
Fewer than ten had survived.
Worse, the way out of the building was buried in rubble and impassable.
They were trapped inside the school.
And enemy planes were still overhead.
Were they just going to wait for the next bomb to fall...? Just as they were thinking that, someone said something.{p}
